author: evergreen reporter
title: Baton Rouge man receives over eight years for illegal gun possession
text:
United States Attorney Kurt Wall announced that Edward Shaffett, 33, from Baton Rouge, Louisiana, has been sentenced to 100 months in federal prison for possessing a firearm as a convicted felon. U.S. Chief Judge Shelly D. Dick also ordered Shaffett to serve three years of supervised release after his prison term and mandated the forfeiture of the firearm involved in the case.
Shaffett admitted that on July 22, 2022, Baton Rouge Police officers found a stolen 2013 Ford Explorer near 7200 Winbourne Avenue. When police tried to stop the vehicle, it fled before coming to a halt. Four people ran from the car; among them was Shaffett, who was carrying a Noreen Firearms .223 caliber AR15 rifle and wearing a black ski mask and gloves.
Police recovered the firearm along Shaffett’s escape route and found an extended AR15 magazine under the driver’s seat of the vehicle. Video footage from a police unit showed Shaffett fleeing with an object resembling an AR15 in his hands.
Shaffett had previously been convicted on April 20, 2021, for possession with intent to distribute oxycodone and attempted illegal possession of a firearm by a felon in Louisiana’s 19th Judicial District Court. He was sentenced then to three years in prison.
The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and Baton Rouge Police Department investigated this case. Assistant United States Attorney Jeremy S. Johnson prosecuted it.
“There is no place for violent criminals with guns on our streets,” said U.S. Attorney Kurt Wall in announcing the sentence.
